test_title: PYST 38: SSC CHSL - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 26 May 2022 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A manufacturer sells an item to a wholesale dealer at a profit of 11%. The wholesaler sells the same to a retailer at a profit of 15%. The retailer in turn sells it to a customer for ₹17,045, thereby earning a profit of 19%. The cost price of the manufacturer is (consider integral part only):
solution:
**Given:**

Item sold to customer by retailer at profit percentage = 19%

Item sold to customer by retailer = Rs 17,045

Profit percentage made by wholesaler by selling an item to retailer = 15%

Profit percentage made by manufacturer by selling an item to wholesale dealer = 11%

**Concept Used:**

Cost Price = 100times(SP)/(100+Profit Percent)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Cost price of the item when the retailer sells an item to a customer = 100times(17045)/(100+19)

⇒ Cost price of the item when the retailer sells an item to a customer = (1704500)/(119)=14,323

⇒ Selling price for the wholesaler who sells to a retailer = Rs 14,323

⇒ Cost Price of an item for wholesaler at a profit of 15% = 100times(14323)/(100+15)

⇒ Cost Price of item for wholesaler at a profit of 15% = (1432300)/(115)=12,455

⇒ Selling price for the manufacturer who sells to wholesale dealer = Rs 12,455

⇒ Cost price of item for the manufacturer at a profit of 11% = 100times(12455)/(100+11)

⇒ Cost price of item for the manufacturer at a profit of 11% = (1245500)/(111)=11,220

**∴ The cost price of an item for the manufacturer is Rs 11,220**
